findings.title: ownerContext's docstring reads as serialising each input reference separately; the source serialises the list once
findings.scenario: Take a transaction with two inputs r1 and r2. The source (mix_logic.ak:127-129) and the definition (definitions.lean:449) both hash serialise_data([r1, r2]): one CBOR list with its framing bytes. Read literally, the docstring's `serialise_data(each input's output_reference)` gives serialise_data(r1) ‖ serialise_data(r2), which has no list framing. A prover built from the doc would hash a different ctx, and every Owner proof would then fail. No transaction makes the definition and the script disagree: this is wording only.
findings.since: present in the extract of Lovejoin/Every/ReadableOwner.lean (git history not read)
findings.evidence: Docstring at definitions.lean:445-446: `blake2b_256(serialise_data(self.outputs) ‖ serialise_data(each input's output_reference) ‖ mix_script_hash)`. Source mix_logic.ak:127-129: `builtin.serialise_data(self.inputs |> list.map(fn(i) { i.output_reference }))`, one call on the whole list. Definition at definitions.lean:449: `Lovejoin.Classic.serialised (.List (tx.txInfoInputs.map fun i => IsData.toData i.txInInfoOutRef))`, also one call on the whole list.
findings.fix: Reword the docstring as `serialise_data(the list of every input's output_reference)`, which matches line 449 and the source.
findings.known_check: None. Only the docstring is affected: the definition at line 449 is right, and it is what ownerResult_typed and validateOwner use.

findings.title: ReadableLaunch's module doc reads as if the output search also requires an inline ReferenceDatum
findings.scenario: The module doc says 'the first output that passes reference.ak's output_at_reference_holder with an inline ReferenceDatum', which reads as one search over both conditions. one_shot_mint.ak:89-99 picks the first output that passes output_at_reference_holder alone. Lines 112-113 then fail if that output's datum is not an inline ReferenceDatum; the search never moves on to a later output. No real transaction tells the two readings apart. The policy mints once, so only one token (P, name) exists, and at most one output can hold quantity 1. So: wording only.
findings.since: present in the extract of Lovejoin/Every/ReadableLaunch.lean (git history not read)
findings.evidence: Module doc at definitions.lean:758-760. Source: one_shot_mint.ak:89-99 (list.find with output_at_reference_holder) and :112-113 (expect InlineDatum, then expect parsed: ReferenceDatum on that target). Definition launchOk at definitions.lean:802-803 matches the source (find? outputAtReferenceHolder, then inlineRefDatum target = some rd), and its own docstring at :796-799 says so correctly.
findings.fix: Reword the module doc as: 'the first output that passes output_at_reference_holder, whose datum must then be an inline ReferenceDatum'.
findings.known_check: None. Only the docstring is affected: launchOk is correct.

guards.stops: A branch challenge c of other than 32 bytes being read as one value by the xor and another by the scalar. xor_bytearray(False, ...) truncates to the shorter operand, so a long c's extra bytes would drop out of the xor constraint, while scalar_from_bytes_mod still reads every byte. A short c makes the xor result too short to equal c_global.
guards.test: sigma_or.ak:229-279 has the fail tests xor_boundary_short_left, _long_right, _31, _33, _64, _empty and _short_last_fold. The definition keeps both length checks: xor32 at definitions.lean:637-640, folded at :662.

guards.stops: A Mix transaction giving the new boxes a stake credential or an attached reference script (H-01/M-01). An output with either one fails the prefix step.
guards.test: No test in the files given. The definition keeps both pins: outputAtScript at definitions.lean:544-548, used by boxOut at :566.

guards.stops: A Mix output holding any value other than the launch's exact box value: a missing token, a wrong quantity, or an extra policy or name. The check is exact Data equality, so it needs no value-shape assumption.
guards.test: No test in the files given. The definition keeps it: boxOut at definitions.lean:566 requires `o.txOutValue = val`, with val = RefDatum.boxValue at :528-532.

checked_ok: mix_logic withdraw dispatch (mix_logic.ak:46-61) matches withdrawOk (definitions.lean:909-913) and mixLogicAccepts (:980-982). The redeemer is cast to MixLogicRedeemer: index 0 Owner or 1 Mix, exactly one List field. Every Owner proof is Constr 0 with exactly [B,B]; every Mix proof is Constr 0 [List], and each branch is Constr 0 with exactly [B,B,B,B]. In the definition this is `red = r.toData` (:443, :628, :634, :903-905). `_account` is never read (`.RewardingScript _`). The reference datum is read before either branch (`∃ rd, readReferenceDatum ...`).

mix_logic publish (mix_logic.ak:70-75) matches :983. RegisterCredential is Certificate constructor 0 in stdlib certificate.ak:11-21, and V3 TxCertRegStaking is Constr 0 (CardanoLedgerApi V3/TxCert.lean:398). The redeemer is Data and is not cast; the certificate's index, credential and deposit are never read.
mix_logic `else(_) { fail }` (mix_logic.ak:77-79) matches `| _ => False` (:984). ScriptInfo indices 0-5 agree (stdlib script_context.ak:34-63 and V3/Contexts.lean:242-249).

read_reference_datum filters every reference input with holds_reference_nft (reference.ak:34-35, :43-45, quantity_of == 1); this matches definitions.lean:329-330 and :336. The stdlib's quantity_of is an ordered dict search (assets.ak:416-430; dict.ak do_get :341-358). On sorted, all-maps values (validTxOutValue, the theorem's hv) it equals the ledger's valueOf. So it matches under hv, which every real reference input meets.
`expect [Input { output, .. }] = carriers` (reference.ak:37) matches `| [c] => ... | _ => none` (:336-338): exactly one carrier.

`expect InlineDatum(d)` then `expect parsed: ReferenceDatum = d` (reference.ak:38-39) matches inlineRefDatum and RefDatum.ofData (:317-326). Both require index 0 and exactly eight fields typed I,B,B,I,I,B,B,B in types.ak:47-56 order, with no length checks on the hash or name bytes. The datum constructor 2 is InlineDatum/OutputDatum on both sides. The raw refFields (Every/Carrier.lean:167-180) also rejects a ninth field.

collect_well_formed_mix_inputs (mix_logic.ak:319-333, with mixbox.ak:30-35 and :78-83) matches collectWellFormedMixInputs, inputAtScript and tryDecodeWellFormedInline (:397-411). Only the input's payment credential is checked; a stake credential or reference script on an input is ignored. stdlib list.filter_map keeps input order (list.ak:488-497), as List.filterMap does. Matches for every input list.

try_decode_well_formed_data with decode_two_byte_fields (mixbox.ak:113-150) matches tryDecodeWellFormedData (:391-394). Both require Constr index 0, exactly two fields, both B, both 48 bytes, and a != b; anything else is None, e.g. Constr 0 [I 1, B b] or a third field.
validate_owner's `n >= 1` and `length(proofs) == n` (mix_logic.ak:117-119) match `boxes ≠ []` (:455) plus AllPairs's equal-length requirement (:50-53).

The Owner ctx (mix_logic.ak:126-133) matches ownerContext (:447-450). Both take serialise_data of the outputs as one ListData and of the list of every input's output_reference (Constr 0 [B txid, I idx]), joined as (o ‖ r) ‖ mix_script_hash, then hashed with blake2b_256.

pairs_match_and_all (mix_logic.ak:341-352) matches AllPairs (:50-53): ([],[]) is True; cons/cons is pred, then recurse; anything else is False. A pred that errors and a pred that returns False both reject, in both branches.

schnorr.verify (schnorr.ak:29-46, with bls.ak:32-76 and hash.ak:25-39) matches Lovejoin/Logic.lean:70-85 (fsHashSchnorr, schnorrVerifies). base, u and t must uncompress. z must be exactly 32 bytes and below q; q at Logic.lean:54 equals bls.ak's hex r, checked. c = blake2b_256(domain ‖ 0x01 ‖ g ‖ u ‖ t ‖ ctx), read big-endian, mod q. The check is equal(z·base, t + c·u), with the same argument order. scalar.from_int is `n % field_prime` (bitwise.ak:133-136), which equals Int.fmod on these non-negative values.
validate_mix's `n >= 2` and `length(proofs) == n` (mix_logic.ak:159-161) match :734.

value.box_value (value.ak:24-36) matches RefDatum.boxValue (:528-532), using stdlib from_asset/from_lovelace (assets.ak:54-66, :124-126: no entry at 0) and add (assets.ak:575-603: unchanged at quantity 0; insert_with puts a non-empty policy after the '' key). The result is an ADA entry if box_lovelace ≠ 0, then (pol, {nm: tq}) unless pol = '' or tq = 0. Matches for every datum, including bl = 0 and zero or negative quantities.
box_value_bytes (mix_logic.ak:189) matches `serialised (.Map rd.boxValue)` (:735). Serialising the Assets newtype gives MapData of its pairs.

walk_outputs (mix_logic.ak:256-310) matches walkOutputs (:581-592). At [] it needs prefix_remaining == 0. `prefix_remaining > 0` is `0 < k`. A prefix step drops k by 1, conses the statement, and appends serialise_data(inline datum) and box_value_bytes. A tail step requires !output_at_script and passes 0.

The prefix step's checks (mix_logic.ak:275-284) match boxOut (:565-576). output_at_script (mixbox.ak:58-67: script hash, stake_credential == None, reference_script == None) is outputAtScript (:544-548). output.value == box_value is exact Data equality. The datum must be InlineDatum. decode_mix_datum_strict (mixbox.ak:101-107: full expect, 48/48, a != b) accepts the same set as tryDecodeWellFormedData; the raw stmtDatum (Every/Walk.lean:104-117) rejects a third field. Both points must uncompress.

Statement points (mix_logic.ak:279-284) match Stmt.toData and branchHolds (:551-559, :649-650). Aiken stores a record's G1Element fields as compressed bytes and uncompresses them on use, so the definition reads uncompress(compress(A)). The module doc discloses this (:498-500). It equals the source's stmt.ap_pt via the BLS fact uncompress(compress(P)) = P.
`list.reverse(statements_rev)` (mix_logic.ak:200) matches `sts.reverse` (:740): statements in output order.
The Mix ctx (mix_logic.ak:202-206) matches :741: blake2b_256((datums ‖ values) ‖ mix_script_hash).

`expect n <= 255` and the header (mix_logic.ak:214-215, hash.ak:93-98: domain ‖ 0x03 ‖ from_int_big_endian(n, 1) = integer_to_bytearray(True, 1, n), bytearray.ak:23-25) match :738-742: `boxes.length ≤ 255`, i2b = integerToByteString true 1 n (Every/Mix.lean:48-51), prefix03 = 'lovejoin/sigmajoin/v1/\x03' (Every/Mix.lean:67).
verify_pre's `expect [_, _, ..] = statements` (sigma_or.ak:139) matches `2 ≤ stmts.length` (:661).

The sigma-OR Fiat-Shamir preimage (sigma_or.ak:148-163, hash.ak:105-113) matches :663-666. stdlib list.foldl is a left fold with callback (elem, acc) (list.ak:932-937). The preimage is header ‖ a ‖ b, then each statement's ap ‖ bp in order, then each branch's t0 ‖ t1 in order, then ctx. The statement bytes are the output datums' raw a and b.

xor32, the v2 fix (sigma_or.ak:77-81), and its fold (:166-172) match xor32 (:637-640) and the foldlM at :662. Both operands must be exactly 32 bytes, else the script fails. The builtin xor runs with False on (acc, br.c), in that order. The fold starts from zero32 (32 zero bytes on both sides; Every/MixPred.lean:182, checked), and its result must equal the hash.
The input points a and b (sigma_or.ak:176-177) must uncompress (:667). An accepting run calls the per-branch closure at least twice, so they are evaluated wherever Aiken places them.

parallel_all and the DH-tuple equations (sigma_or.ak:182-219) match branchHolds and AllPairs (:646-654, :668). They walk in lockstep, and a length mismatch is False. t0 and t1 must uncompress. z goes through scalar_from_bytes (32 bytes, below q; scalarOf at Every/Shared.lean:123-128). c goes through scalar_from_bytes_mod (any length, mod q; scalarMod at Shared.lean:131). The checks are z·a == t0 + c·a' and z·b == t1 + c·b', with g1.scale = scalar_mul(to_int k, p). The `&&` short-circuit only skips work on a rejecting path.

The launch datum (one_shot_mint.ak:112-113) matches inlineRefDatum (:803): an inline datum, then the full ReferenceDatum cast, on the found output only. A bad datum there rejects, with no fallback to a later output.

datum_sane and token_sane (one_shot_mint.ak:114-119, :143-157, :161) match datumSane (:790-794): 0 < box_lovelace; 0 < max_fee; max_fee < box_lovelace. If the policy is '', the name is '' and the quantity 0; otherwise the policy is 28 bytes, the name at most 32 bytes, and 0 < q ≤ 18446744073709551615 (= 2^64 − 1, checked).

The final `and` (one_shot_mint.ak:121-126) matches :804-805: the seed spent, the name 'lovejoin' (#6c6f76656a6f696e decodes to lovejoin; lovejoinName at Every/MintSpec.lean:23), quantity 1, and the datum sane.

mix_box has no definition in the extract, so I checked it against Lovejoin/AnyTx/BoxPurposesAll.lean:53-62 (contextPasses), with BoxSemantics.lean:102-105 (datumPassesLedger), Common.lean:65-67 (isBoxDatum) and BoxCover.lean:17-21. The source's list.find for the first input whose output_reference == utxo, then `expect Some` (mix_box.ak:52-55), matches `inputPairs = before ++ (toData ref, …) :: after` with no earlier pair at ref. An inline, well-formed datum needs pairs.has_key(withdrawals, Script(mix_logic_script_hash)), i.e. the key at any position with any amount (mix_box.ak:57-70). The definition says `isBoxDatum d = false ∨ ∃ amount, (ScriptCredential L, amount) ∈ wdrl`. NoDatum and DatumHash pass on both sides, and `else(_) { fail }` (:73-75) is `| _ => False`. The datum and redeemer are not cast. Matches for every typed context, with no value hypothesis.
The withdrawal amount: neither mix_logic nor mix_box reads it (mix_box needs only the key present), and neither definition constrains it.

mix_box's gate and mix_logic's collection use the same well-formedness. isBoxDatum (Common.lean:65-67, wellFormed at Logic.lean:57-58) holds exactly when tryDecodeWellFormedData (:391-394) is some, as try_decode_well_formed_data is shared by mix_box.ak:59 and mixbox.ak:80.
notes: definitions.lean has no mix_box definition: it contains no mix_box or spend clause, though the task describes it as covering mix_box. The repo's typed mix_box rule is contextPasses (Lovejoin/AnyTx/BoxPurposesAll.lean:53-62). It sits outside the Readable layer and is stated over raw Data pairs (inputPairs = before ++ (toData ref, Constr 0 [addr, value, toData datum, script]) :: after), not in the source's terms (list.find over typed inputs). I checked it against mix_box.ak and it matches (see checked_ok). But a claim that the Readable layer covers all three validators would be wrong.

No semantic mismatch in mix_logic or one_shot_mint. Two clauses match only under the theorems' stated hypotheses: hv (every reference input's value is validTxOutValue) for mix_logic, and hmint/houts (the mint is validMintValue, every output validTxOutValue) for one_shot_mint. They are needed only where the source uses the stdlib's ordered dict search: quantity_of in holds_reference_nft and output_at_reference_holder, and assets.tokens on the mint. Every real Conway transaction meets them. `output.value == box_value` in walk_outputs is exact Data equality and needs no hypothesis.

The one place the definitions read differently from the source is disclosed (definitions.lean:498-500). branchHolds uses uncompress(compress(A')) because Aiken stores a record's G1Element fields as compressed bytes. This equals the source's A' only through the BLS fact uncompress(compress(P)) = P, which the definitions don't assume. A claim stated with A' should cite that fact.

mix_logic's theorems fix reference_nft_name to nftName = 'lovejoin', while the script itself takes the name as a parameter. one_shot_mint pins that name, so every v2 launch is covered. A mix_logic applied with any other name is outside the statements.

Two things match the source but are outside what the definitions guarantee, by design. First, neither mix_logic nor mix_box reads the withdrawal amount. Second, one_shot_mint doesn't check the datum's three script hashes; its source says so at one_shot_mint.ak:102-105. So a launch whose mix_script_hash isn't the deployed mix_box would leave boxes gated on mix_logic but never collected by it. That is a launch-time property, not a definition mismatch.

Independence. I read only definitions, the stdlib and the ledger and PlutusCore types. A few sed ranges around looked-up definitions also printed nearby proof lines: Every/Shared.lean ap_lessThanEquals, Every/Mix.lean apleft_i2b, AnyTx/BoxSemantics.lean (found_iff's statement and datumPasses_ledger's 5-line proof), and the start of every_context_iff in BoxPurposesAll.lean. I didn't use them. On how Aiken v1.1.24 compiles a cast (index check, exact arity), my reading of Aiken's full expect agrees with the raw specs the extract names: Every/Walk.lean stdmtDatum, Every/Carrier.lean refFields/carrierDatum, Every/MintSpec.lean outDatum, Every/Withdraw.lean ownerProof/mixBranchOk/mixProof. Those raw specs belong to the proof chain, so that one point is not fully independent of it.

reference_holder.ak (always False) has no readable definition here and none was asked for. fee_contract is out of scope. Not checked: the docstring at definitions.lean:867-871 on validScriptContext's isBalanced, which concerns the ledger model, not the source.
coverage: I compared every clause of mix_logic.ak (withdraw, publish, else, validate_owner, validate_mix, walk_outputs, collect_well_formed_mix_inputs, pairs_match_and_all), one_shot_mint.ak (mint, token_sane, else) and mix_box.ak (spend, else). That includes the helpers they call in reference.ak, mixbox.ak, value.ak, schnorr.ak, sigma_or.ak, hash.ak and bls.ak, and the stdlib v4.0.0 code behind them: list filter, filter_map, find, any, foldl, reverse, length and map; dict get_or_else, do_get, insert_with, singleton and to_pairs; assets from_asset, from_lovelace, add, quantity_of and tokens; bytearray concat, length and from_int_big_endian; scalar and bitwise from_int; g1 scale, add and equal; pairs.has_key; and the Transaction, Output, Datum, Address, Credential, Certificate and ScriptInfo types. I compared them against every definition in definitions.lean (lines 50-150, 299-458, 528-742, 783-805, 899-913, 980-984, 1010-1013). I also read the repo definitions the extract names but doesn't give: Logic.lean q, wellFormed, serialised, fsHashSchnorr and schnorrVerifies; Shared.lean scalarOf and scalarMod; Mix.lean i2b and prefix03; MixPred.lean zero32; nftName; lovejoinName; isRegistrationData. On the ledger side I read TxInfo, TxInInfo, TxOut, OutputDatum, Address, Credential, StakingCredential, ScriptInfo, the TxCert encodings, TxOutRef's BEq, Value, valueOf, validTxOutValue, V3 validMintValue, Withdrawals and toTerm; on the PlutusCore side, ByteString, the G1 builtins, integerToByteString and byteStringToInteger. I checked the constants zero32, q, 2^64 − 1 and the 'lovejoin' hex. mix_box I checked against the repo's contextPasses, because the extract has none. Not done: no Lean build, no reading of compiled UPLC, no proofs read on purpose; reference_holder and fee_contract not compared.
